name: lance_core::utils::deletion::OffsetMapper::map_offset
behavior: map_offset starts mid=offset+last_diff and right=offset+deletion count cast to u32. Each loop counts deleted offsets in 0..mid+1 and compares mid with offset+deleted_count. Equality with an undeleted mid stores last_diff=mid-offset and returns. Less asserts left!=mid+1, advances left=mid+1, then bisects [left,right]; greater or equality at a deleted mid moves right=mid and bisects. The comment explains leftward search for an overshooting guess. left persists across calls and is not reset on success; input monotonicity is not checked. Additions, subtraction, mid+1 and cardinality cast have no checked-error path, so near-u32-limit inputs can overflow under checked arithmetic or wrap otherwise. No validation rejects ordinals past actual fragment rows because that length is absent. With Set, every range-cardinality step scans 0..mid+1, a potentially large cost unrelated to set cardinality.

behavior: zip_into_one consumes buffers paired with bit widths and a u64 value count. It rejects widths not divisible by8 with InvalidInput including the width; zero width is accepted. Unsafe zipper loops until output pointer reaches end, copies each source width with copy_nonoverlapping and advances both pointers. For valid inputs it interleaves rows in supplied buffer order and ignores surplus source tails. Safety requires each source contain every requested value and all size/address arithmetic fit; these are not established by this safe public function. Short inputs or overflow can cause out-of-bounds raw access, not merely a Result error. No unsafe probe was executed. Empty buffers, zero rows or all-zero widths produce empty output. name: lance_encoding::data::arrow_dictionary_to_data_block
behavior: arrow_dictionary_to_data_block first concatenates dictionaries and derives actual key count. If logical validity exists, it reuses the first null dictionary item or appends a null item. A null-item index beyond current key maximum widens keys to UInt32; inability beyond that limit is unimplemented. This can happen with either a new or existing null dictionary item. For nullable dictionaries, conversion encodes the null index in the chosen key type, copies key bytes and replaces every logically invalid row key. Validity is moved into the dictionary items; the fixed indices carry no validity bitmap. Without logical validity it clones key bytes. Dictionary items recursively convert through DataBlock::from, and key stats start empty.

name: lance_encoding::data::DataBlock::from_arrays
behavior: Public infallible from_arrays returns AllNull0 when arrays is empty or declared count is0 before inspecting nonempty input type/nulls. It uses only first datatype, computes logical nullability and returns AllNull with declared count for all-null input. Classic Binary/Utf8 use32-bit normalization, Large variants64; BinaryView/Utf8View cast to classic32-bit with expect. Boolean uses packed fixed-width1. Fixed-size binary, integer/unsigned, floats16/32/64, dates, times, timestamps, intervals, durations and decimals32/64/128/256 use raw fixed-width copy. Null yields AllNull. Dictionary uses key/null normalization. Declared count and actual copied lengths can disagree for misuse of this public infallible API. Struct conversion collects each positional child across all input arrays and recursively converts using declared row count. It stores parent validity on StructDataBlock. Generic wrapping later also creates Nullable for Some, so a partially nullable Struct can retain parent validity in both inner and outer representations. Child type/shape agreement is assumed. FixedSizeList conversion collects child values, recursively converts declared_count*dimension and wraps dimension cast to u64. List/LargeList/ListView/LargeListView/Map/RunEndEncoded/Union are unsupported panics unless zero/all-null shortcuts already returned. Unsupported logical type does not imply every invocation panics. from_arrays computes statistics on the encoded inner representation, then wraps Some validity in Nullable with a fresh empty outer BlockInfo. Dictionaries skip this wrapper because nulls were normalized into items. Statistics may recurse into children or require existing child stats; Struct stats sum child MaxLength and can panic when a child lacks it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:56-71; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:579-597)

name: lance_encoding::encoder::encode_batch
behavior: Public async encode_batch is a memory helper primarily for tests/benchmarks/IPC, not a complete Lance file serializer. It rejects non-power-of-two or alignment<8 via InvalidInput. The is_pwr_two call executes first: n-1 underflows for0 with overflow checks enabled, so zero can panic before the intended Result; without overflow checks the subsequent minimum test rejects it. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:15-16) Derive encoding schema from batch.schema(), force keep_original_array=true regardless of supplied option, construct encoders, then prepare all root arrays before maybe_encode. Preparation errors return before any maybe_encode, subject to custom prepare implementations honoring no-mutation. Supplied Arc<Schema> is not used for dispatch or checked for agreement; it is returned later unchanged. Process roots sequentially. Start external reservation at current byte length, use fresh RepDefBuilder and row_number0, maybe_encode then flush before awaiting any task. Append external payload buffers without their reserved padding; await tasks in vector order and bucket PageInfo by encoded_page.column_idx. This helper introduces no concurrent task polling or spawn, although tasks may encapsulate work already dispatched by encoders. After all tasks for a root complete, create fresh external reservation, await finish, append returned external buffers unpadded, then serialize each column-scoped buffer unpadded while recording offsets/actual sizes. Column enumeration uses cumulative count of previous finish results, not returned mapping or encoder.num_columns. Append each EncodedColumn.final_pages to the bucket identified by each page column_idx, then remove pages for current enumerated physical column into ColumnInfo. Missing bucket yields empty pages. Buckets with unreported indices or pages arriving after their column was removed can remain discarded at root-loop end. Correct ordering/index membership is an implicit strategy contract, not validated. top_level_columns collects every allocated mapping index and discards field IDs, including nested leaf allocations; it is not necessarily one index per schema root. Freeze Bytes and return supplied schema plus batch row count. All intermediate Result errors propagate; no partial EncodedBatch is returned. Dropping the future drops its local state and unawaited task futures; behavior of already spawned codec work is outside this helper.

behavior: V2 maybe_encode requires StructArray then BlobV2Layout::Prepared, otherwise InvalidInput with actual dtype or classified/unrecognized layout. Classifier is called twice on rejection. Read kind UInt8,data LargeBinary,uri Utf8,blob_id UInt32,blob_size UInt64,position UInt64 by name, with contextual missing-field errors then infallible typed casts. Shape classification normally proves types/names; direct row null/value requirements remain unchecked. Allocate five output builders by row count, URI capacity row_count*16 unchecked. Parent-null OR kind-null row emits valid placeholder child values Inline/0/0/0/empty URI; output later preserves only parent null bitmap, so a null kind under valid parent becomes a valid empty-looking inline descriptor. Dedicated emits kind,position0,raw blob_size/blob_id and empty URI, ignoring those child validities. External copies URI even if its validity is null, defaults missing position/size/base-id child values to0, otherwise copies them. Packed directly copies position/blob_size/blob_id without checking their validity and emits empty URI. No URI validation, sidecar existence, positive size/ID, offset bounds or checked range arithmetic here. Unknown nonnull kind fails BlobKind::try_from. Inline directly reads data even if child null, copies bytes to external-buffer collector even when empty, stores reserved position/length and id0/empty URI. Append all output children as nonnull values. Earlier rows can already have appended external buffers when a later unknown kind fails. No local rollback. Finish builders and create five-field descriptor StructArray with cloned original parent nulls only; pass original repdef,row metadata and collector to descriptor encoder. No BlobLayout wrapper or original-binary sentinel scheme. V2 null structure is ordinary Arrow parent validity.

One large blob can exceed target; null/empty rows consume no byte budget and can accumulate without a row bound. Flush final nonempty descriptor vector, even with zero read ranges. name: lance_encoding::encodings::logical::primitive::chunk_index::parse_nested_rep
behavior: parse_nested_rep consumes little-endian u64 words using stride words per chunk. num_chunks floors (bytes.len()/8)/stride; zero stride divides by zero, stride one can overlap words then overrun, and trailing bytes/incomplete groups are not locally rejected. Only first two words per group are read: ends and partial. has_trailer=partial>0; starts=ends+trailer-previous_trailer; accumulate starts into prefix and set trailer bit. Arithmetic unchecked, deeper-level words ignored, and no final-trailer, row total or cross-axis count validation. Caller comment about divisible-by-eight alone is insufficient for stride one. Empty input with positive stride yields prefix[0] and empty bits.

behavior: ConstantPageScheduler stores type, meanings, maximum repetition/visible levels, buffer layout and optional cache state. Constructor counts list meanings then casts to u16; max_visible_level is delegated. Inline bytes are copied. Positions plus sizes form ranges using unchecked addition. Accepted layouts: inline with zero buffers, inline with two rep/def buffers, external with one value buffer, external with three value/rep/def buffers. Inline with other counts is InvalidInput. Zero-sized rep/def buffers become None; external value buffer remains a required scalar range even when empty. No-inline zero buffers is missing scalar InvalidInput; two is ambiguous InvalidInput; other unexpected counts rejected. Constructor stores state with no cached data. It does not decode/validate inline bytes, array length, level counts/values, alignment or file bounds.

behavior: Generic variable-width dictionary helper borrows block bytes, typed offsets and U8SliceKey map entries. Stat MaxLength must exist and be a UInt64 array; expect panics otherwise. Initial payload capacity is saturating32*max_length, at least1024, then bounded by source data and target budget. Indices reserve declared num_values. No complete offset-count/first-zero/final-end validation. Iterate every physical adjacent offset pair; conversion to usize, descending offsets or end beyond data return None. Nonzero first offset or unused trailing data are accepted. Exact byte strings map to first-seen signed i32 IDs. New entry requires positive max_entries, current unique count below it and below i32::MAX. Payload is extended before output-offset conversion and size checks, so rejected attempts still allocate transiently. After each index, estimated encoded size is saturating payload bytes +4*index count +offset-width*(unique count+1). Return None only when greater than max_encoded_size, allowing equality. This is an output-size filter, not peak-memory bound: map, preallocation, stats and allocations before checks are excluded. No loop iterations bypasses this in-loop size check. Successful variable-width result has dictionary offsets/data and unique count with matching32/64 offset width, plus FixedWidth indices with32 bits and declared input num_values. Statistics are recomputed for both. Physical window count is not compared with declared num_values, so malformed blocks can yield inconsistent counts.

name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::binary::search_next_offset_idx
behavior: search_next_offset_idx is private generic and takes last position and i64 budget. Remaining<=1 returns offsets.len()-1. Otherwise initialize accepted count2 and candidate4; one-value nonfinal chunks cannot be represented because log0 denotes the final chunk. Budget is an aim, not a hard bound: the initial two values need not fit. If candidate reaches/passes end, return full remainder when its data plus offset table fits; otherwise keep last accepted power of two. This tail-fit branch bypasses MAX_MINIBLOCK_VALUES. For a fitting normal candidate, check candidate*2>cached maximum BEFORE accepting candidate. Thus normal cap4096 can stop at2048; a fitting tail can exceed cap, and initial2 exceeds cap1. Alignment padding is outside the budget estimate; negative target still permits initial2. No Result validation or overflow guard.

name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::bitpacking::bitpack_out_of_line
behavior: Private generic bitpack_out_of_line borrows full typed payload and derives number of chunks/remainder from physical typed length, ignoring FixedWidthDataBlock.num_values. Compute ceil(1024*W/data.bits_per_value) native output words; allocate num_chunks*words capacity. If widths/counts/arithmetic are malformed, no Result validation here. This is headerless per1024 packing at one configured W. For each full physical1024 chunk, unsafe pack into exact spare slice, set_len after guaranteed initialization. name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::byte_stream_split::<ByteStreamSplitEncoder as MiniBlockCompressor>::compress
behavior: Mini compress requires FixedWidth else InvalidInputSource. Uses configured width and input logical count without checking block width, exact data length or Arrow numeric type. Count0 returns no buffers/no chunks and BSS(Flat(configwidth,None)), discarding any provided bytes. For positive count allocate count-as-usize*bytewidth zero bytes unchecked. For each chunk n up to hardcoded maximum, transpose input[(processed+i)*width+j] into output[chunk_offset+j*n+i]. Short input panics, extra input ignored; width disagreement can reinterpret/lose bytes. Runtime cost O(count*width), one full output allocation. Record each payload size n*width; final chunk always log0 even when full, nonfinal log10/9. Return one concatenated buffer, metadata and original count. No local padding; nested Flat optional compressionNone and TODO for underlying compression. Every chunk must be separated before inverse.

name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::general::<GeneralMiniBlockCompressor as MiniBlockCompressor>::compress
behavior: Private MIN_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_COMPRESSION=4096 bytes. compress first delegates owned page and unchanged context to inner. If data is empty or first whole buffer length<4096, return inner result and descriptor unchanged before factory validation. Equality attempts compression. Threshold is aggregate first-buffer size, not each chunk or sum of all buffers. Inner errors propagate. After threshold, obtain one outer codec for the page or return its error. For each inner chunk index buffer_sizes[0], slice first data buffer by cumulative offset, append compressed chunk bytes, compute output length delta asu32, clone size vector and replace only element0 while preserving log count. Missing first size or invalid range panics; arithmetic and narrowing are unchecked. Assumes chunk sizes exactly cover first input buffer; accepted path drops any unaccounted trailing bytes. Other buffers are not compressed. Context flags are passed inward but not used to revalidate compressed sizes. If summed compressed bytes>=summed original chunk bytes, discard scratch data/chunks and return original result/descriptor. Equality and zero total fall back. Acceptance is strict aggregate savings; one chunk may grow if others compensate. Trace ratio is f32 diagnostic only. Work and temporary memory have already been spent before fallback. On acceptance replace buffer0 with compressed bytes, move all remaining original buffers unchanged, preserve num_values and store rewritten chunk sizes. Wrap selected CompressionConfig around the original encoding using ProtobufUtils21::wrapped; descriptor conversion may error after compression. Retains selected optional level rather than runtime-normalized codec config. Page input, compressed scratch and cloned metadata coexist during work; no strict allocation cap. Noop typically falls back for equal size; unsupported factory config may remain unobserved on small pages.

name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::rle::RleDecompressor::decode_generic
behavior: Generic eager expansion accepts an empty child only with expected count zero; positive count with either empty child errors. Nonempty input validates paired sizes, borrows typed values, checked-converts logical count to usize and try_reserve_exact allocates the expanded vector. Allocation failure becomes InvalidInput. Historical mini runs may cross checkpoints, so mini decoding clamps overflow while block decoding rejects it. No version tag gates this behavior. Every physical run rejects zero and checked-converts length. Strict overflow returns InvalidInput. Clamping overflow fills the remaining logical values and stops, ignoring subsequent entries. Final underflow errors. If exact coverage was already reached, a following zero still errors; a following positive entry triggers a zero-length clamp and stops. Trace logs count/type; initialized values are reinterpreted without unsafe set_len.

behavior: chunk_fsl estimates validity bytes per outer row as sum ceil(cumulative_dimension/8) for present buffers; computes leaf bits times product of dimensions. Byte-aligned rows use one row/word, otherwise eight; add estimated validity bytes scaled by word rows, then reuse chunk selector. Preallocate chunk vector for ceil(rows/rows_per_chunk). Thus comment about allocating sufficient padding does not establish exact preallocation: capacities can grow later. Input validity length is compared only in debug assertion against that larger estimate. Walk complete outer-row chunks, append each layer validity slice and size vector, emit positive log; emit residual rows with log0 only if nonzero. Build nested descriptor; output data vector is all concatenated validity buffers in outer-to-inner order followed by the moved original leaf buffer. num_values is outer row count. A complete final chunk keeps its positive log. Buffers are parallel across chunks, not row-major. No payload/size-total validation or IO.

name: lance_encoding::encodings::physical::value::ValueEncoder::nullable_per_value_fsl
behavior: nullable_per_value_fsl instead tracks current FSL correctly, multiplying each dimension. For each Nullable child reserve ceil(cumulative_dim/8) bytes per outer row and collect bit iterator. Nested lists continue with their own dimension. FixedWidth terminal computes data bytes per row as ceil(inner_bits/8)*cum_dim, not ceil(inner_bits*cum_dim/8); therefore it assumes byte-expanded inner items on this route. Raw bitpacked Boolean payload can violate that size expectation unless normalized by callers; complete normalization trace pending. All integer casts/products unchecked. AllNull terminal synthesizes all-zero validity sized ceil(cum_dim/8)*num_rows, sets leaf byte width0 and empty data buffer. This deliberately avoids zero per-row full-zip width when positive dimensions and rows have no control bytes. If a Nullable wrapper was already collected at this same terminal layer, another validity iterator is appended while descriptor has only one has_validity flag; unusual directly constructed nested wrappers are not validated here. Unsupported children unreachable. Allocate row-major output capacity bytes_per_row*num_values. For each row append each validity bit slice (byte-padded per row), advance its bit offset, then append exact leaf data slice for that row. name: lance_encoding::EncodingsIo
behavior: Public EncodingsIo:Debug+Send+Sync supplies a single-file IO service without requiring lance-io. submit_request borrows self, owns Vec<Range<u64>> and u64 priority, and returns a static boxed future of Result<Vec<Bytes>>. Contract requires one returned Bytes per requested range even after coalescing, and an empty buffer for each empty range. Priority should be the lowest row delivered so late indirect reads can be prioritized. Trait declaration does not enforce range legality, response ordering/count, scheduling, cancellation or durability; implementations/callers own those obligations. Default submit_single owns one range/priority, calls submit_request immediately, maps Ok through v.pop().unwrap(), then boxes. Upstream Err is preserved. An empty success vector panics while the mapped future is polled; surplus responses silently drop all but the last. No response-count validation or buffer-size check occurs. Correct one-response implementations return their sole Bytes. Default with_bypass_backpressure returns None. Contract describes a derived IO service for indirect reads to avoid backpressure deadlock/latency; unsupported callers should fall back to self. This default neither clones a service nor changes scheduling. Default with_io_stats accepts Arc<dyn IoStatsRecorder> but ignores/drops it and returns None. Docs describe additive per-scope accounting without reopening files; unsupported callers fall back to self without scope statistics. No counters, wrapper, global accounting or instrumentation are created here.

callees: Four required/default IO hooks.

It does no compression or feature check. packed_struct moves ordered child descriptors and a present packed Page buffer reference. name: lance_encoding::repdef::RepDefBuilder::concat_layers
behavior: concat_layers gathers same-depth raw layers across batches, computing bitmap presence, cumulative slots/specials and empty flags. Layer kind and FSL dimension are taken from encountered inputs, effectively last input; homogeneous kinds/dimensions are documented assumptions, not validated. Without null bitmaps, plain validity and FSL return count-only descriptors. Otherwise allocate a bitmap; offsets allocate a vector starting0 even with no nulls. Capacity is a hint, not exact storage enforcement. Concatenate optional validity, filling true for missing bitmaps when needed. Offset vectors append all but initial0 after adding previous tail. FSL bitmap concatenation follows slot counts; no dimension consistency check. Finish normalized descriptor by selected kind. Public serialize consumes nonempty builder vector through normalize then dense serialization. normalize asserts nonempty, debug-asserts equal layer counts, indexes each builder at first-builder depths, concatenates once and marks all-valid only if every builder.is_empty. Fewer layers can panic; extra layers can be ignored in release.

name: lance_encoding::repdef::RepDefUnraveler::unravel_offsets
behavior: unravel_offsets delegates sparse first. Dense requires rep vector and list meaning, advances layer/def counters, identifies null/empty levels, then scans outward through adjacent item meanings to include null structs masking this list. This call handles list validity together with offsets. Append offsets after existing tail by reading tail then popping it, avoiding duplicate boundaries between pages. T::from_usize failure returns InvalidInput mentioning i32::MAX/large containers even though T is generic. State/counters and destination may already be mutated before failure; no rollback contract. Dense paired loop asserts equal lengths then uses unchecked reads/writes with read_idx<len and write_idx<=read_idx. Only nonzero rep starts survive, decremented by1. Invisible outer entries remain in compacted levels but emit no offsets. Valid starts add one child; null/empty/masked starts add zero and bitmap false/true; rep0 continues child count. Truncate both vectors to local surviving starts. Rep-only loop emits each nonzero start, compacts/decrements rep, counts every input as child, appends final tail and truncates to THIS unraveler write_idx, not cumulative destination lists. If another page required validity, append true for locally produced lists. This preserves nested multi-page reconstruction.

name: lance_encoding::repdef::SerializerContext::normalize_specials_and_plan_splits
behavior: Split planner early exits: no defs, no rep, absent budget, zero visible values, any FSL, or no variable-list meaning. Existing defs are normalized on all exits except already-empty defs. If both buffers exist, unequal lengths returns Internal before budget checks. WithinBudget is conditional policy, not a universal byte-size guarantee. Planner tracks row and page dense ranges and visible counts. A row has overhead iff dense entries exceed visible values. Record over-budget count only for rows with overhead; last offending row overwrites prior count. Greedily split before a row only if current page nonempty, either side has overhead and combined levels exceed budget. Dense-only long rows are exempt from this policy. Normalize each special while scanning equal buffers. Top row starts exactly when rep equals schema list count. Levels before a top-row start, absent starts, or a first discovered start after position0 return Internal. Count visible defs<=threshold and finish final row. Input state can already be normalized when error occurs; serializer is consumed by caller. Counted top rows and visible values must equal supplied counts or Internal includes expected/actual. No overhead returns WithinBudget; any offending row returns SingleRowOverBudget before page-split result. Otherwise append final split and require more than one split for RequiresPageSplit. Does not emit pages or choose fallback codec.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::bench_random_access
behavior: bench_random_access defines filesystems[mem,disk], one current-thread global runtime without enable_all and one TempDir, creates take group, and chooses V2_0,V2_1,V2_2 only. Current runtime handles spawn_blocking coordination, while cached per-reader current-thread runtimes execute read_task. No direct benchmark-specific environment lookup in this file; CPU/env effects enter the helper. For each store/version get cached readers before registering cases. Cartesian loops choose multithreaded false/true, rows_at_a_time1/100 and cached true/false, skipping nocache for mem or V2_0. Nominal32 random-access registrations:12mem and20disk; if compute T=1 both thread-mode names coincide, and duplicate-name handling is Criterion-dependent/unverified. Active multithread uses cached compute count T, otherwise1. Throughput Elements advertises T*floor(100000/T); it does not account for later rows_at_a_time truncation. Actual parallel count is T*g*floor(floor(100000/T)/g), where g is1 or100; single-thread uses full100000 selectors, divisible by both active g. name: lance_file::concat::check_compatibility
behavior: check_compatibility first rejects any Blob in the ordinary target schema, then requires a first prepared input. It derives the baseline physical columns from the first input, descriptor-projects the target only for part mode, and serializes all baseline column encodings before checking input row/version/schema. It does not itself reject target V1; public ordinary dispatch handles legacy earlier. Per-input check order is expected footer rows(InvalidInput), exact version(Unsupported VersionMismatch), complete Schema equality(Unsupported SchemaMismatch), exact external-metadata validation(CorruptFile wrapping any delegated error), then normalized/footer row equality(CorruptFile). No coercion, alias equivalence, column reordering or semantic encoding comparison is attempted. After metadata validation, more than one global buffer gives Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers; schema buffer0 is regenerated. Different column count versus the first input gives ColumnLayoutMismatch(None), although prior schema/metadata checks may reject first. A zero-global buffer case has no local rejection here; valid readers normally require schema storage upstream. Each physical column must have no column-level buffers, the same index as baseline and identical serialized column-level encoding. Error order is ColumnBuffers then index layout then encoding mismatch. Different page encodings/page counts are allowed if preceding validation succeeds. Returns None after every input; it never reads page payloads or validates their absolute ranges against EOF.

name: lance_file::concat::copy_page_buffers
behavior: copy_page_buffers allocates output PageInfo capacity equal to page count and groups consecutive complete pages. For each page, checked offset+size rejects u64 range overflow and checked sum(size) rejects page byte-count overflow as contextual CorruptFile with path,input,column,page. There is no local offset+size<=file_size check; subsequent scheduler IO determines out-of-file behavior. A page after the first in a batch is deferred when checked cumulative bytes overflow or exceed read_batch_bytes. The first page is always admitted, even oversized. The aggregate addition is then checked. Buffer counts include zero lengths but read ranges omit them; positive offset+size arithmetic is safe only because the earlier checked pass succeeded. Page boundaries/order are preserved, with no sorting/coalescing here. One scheduler request at priority0 returns all positive-length ranges in the batch, or no IO occurs if none. Consume one returned Bytes per nonempty buffer; missing response or unequal byte length is contextual IO error, including overlong results under the short-read wording. Zero buffers consume no result but still call writer.write_external_buffer(empty). Each buffer is written sequentially and its new offset/size retained. After writing all buffers of each page, clone its encoding, preserve num_rows and checked-add whole-input row_offset to priority. Priority overflow is InvalidInput after possible output writes. Extra returned buffers are rejected only after the batch writes. Retain relocated PageInfo for all pages; no page decoding, retry, checksum or rollback occurs in this helper.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::binary::BinaryDecoder::take
behavior: decode delegates get(..). Public take documents sorted indices, returns a typed empty array before IO for empty input, otherwise uses first/last values to request the full position span. MIN_IO_SIZE is fixed at 64*1024 bytes; TODOs leave it nonconfigurable and position reads unchunked. end+1 uses u32 arithmetic before conversion. Unsorted, nullable or out-of-bounds indices are not validated here. Compute exact intended payload capacity by iterating every index, unwrapping its validity and summing adjacent position differences relative to the first index. Null indices panic here. Allocate payload and (N+1)*offset-width buffers, initialize zero offset using unchecked push. The safety comment relies on sufficient precomputed capacity; length/product/difference overflow and negative persisted positions remain unchecked. Duplicate indices contribute their payload lengths repeatedly to capacity. Plan chunks, issue each enclosing byte-array range through get_range and poll with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism()). A contiguous chunk copies value_data once, while a noncontiguous chunk copies each requested value. Both append a cumulative offset per requested index with unsafe push_unchecked under the capacity assumption. Repeated-leading [k,k] with a nonempty value becomes a contiguous [0,0] chunk: only one value span is copied but two offsets are accumulated. Ordered buffering preserves planned output order; it does not spawn detached tasks or add error/cancellation cleanup. After IO, build output offsets and debug-assert copied payload bytes equal the precomputed capacity. The repeated-leading nonempty-value trace violates that assertion in debug builds; without it, inconsistent final offsets reach fallible array building. When nullable, equal output offsets again determine validity. Return a new materialized payload array. No guarantee is claimed for malformed inputs or release behavior beyond the observed builder call.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::page_table::PageTable::write
behavior: write documents dense placeholders. Reject completely empty outer map with InvalidInput source empty page table. Then reject supplied min_field_id>observed minimum with InvalidInput whose message uses field_id_offset. Take observed max and build inclusive[min,max]. Lower min is allowed to include ancestor/hole fields; all checks here precede writer.tell. Await writer.tell for start position, then find maximum batch key across all inner maps, unwrap it, and add1. Nonempty outer/all-empty inner maps panic at unwrap after tell; batch-ID max overflow and casts are unchecked. Int64Builder capacity is field_count*num_batches, although two values will be appended per cell, so it underestimates final element count. No dimensions are persisted in this method. Iterate field-major then batch0..num_batches. Existing PageInfo appends position and length cast to i64; missing pair appends[0,0]. Finish Int64Array and write_all its first Arrow buffer directly, then return prior tell position. No explicit endian conversion, alignment, length prefix, footer, flush/shutdown or atomic/abort guard appears. A partial write/error/cancellation can leave output bytes; successful return is not publication/durability. A table whose only batch key is-1 derives0batches and writes an empty buffer; more negative/overflowed dimensions remain unchecked.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::read_list_array
behavior: read_list_array expands Range end and RangeTo end by1 for the terminal offset; Indices reads the entire first..last+2 position interval. RangeFull/from pass through unchanged. List position lookup deliberately uses reader.page_table rather than the page_table argument, then reads T::DATA_TYPE (Int32/Int64) with the PageInfo position and length. Children later use the supplied table. This distinction matters if invoked with a statistics or other alternate table; no local assertion ensures equality. The position result is downcast to the generic primitive type. Map logical list selectors to child rows: Range uses first and range-length endpoint; To uses0..positions[end]; From uses first position..child end; Full uses first..last position; Indices returns take_list_array. Ranges has an Internal error branch, but ordinary fixed-stride decoding rejects that selector earlier. Position access, range subtraction and child bounds are delegated/unchecked rather than preflighted. Subtract first absolute position from all offsets with Arrow arithmetic, recursively read children[0] over derived child selector using the supplied page table, and call try_new_generic_list_array. Parent validity and original child field metadata are not passed. Arrow arithmetic/building errors propagate; no local offset monotonicity, nonnegativity or payload-length check precedes them.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::reader::take_list_array
behavior: Generic take_list_array expects a nonempty sorted UInt32 selector. It subtracts the first selector from every raw selector value and indexes the already fetched position span to create per-list child ranges. Null selector validity is ignored, and unsigned subtraction, positions and first-child existence are unchecked. It clones the Field and accumulates arrays rather than streaming child values. For each selected list range, await read_array on children[0] sequentially, so repeated indices cause repeated child reads at this layer. Retain all arrays, build offsets from summed range lengths with unchecked addition/conversion, concatenate all values, and build a generic list. No separate list validity is restored; the helper creates an all-valid List/LargeList with child named item and nullable=true from the actual value type (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229). This does not preserve arbitrary original child metadata or nullability.

behavior: truncate_binary asserts input length>=requested length and always returns Some(exact prefix of that length), including zero; there is no all-maximal-byte special case despite the adjacent comment. increment performs big-endian-style carry from the last byte: overflow writes0 and continues left, first nonoverflow returns the same-length vector. name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::truncate_utf8
behavior: truncate_utf8 asserts data.len()>=length, walks char_indices backward over the original entire string, and returns the longest NONEMPTY valid prefix whose ending byte offset is <=length. It returns None when no full character fits, including length0; it never manufactures Some(empty). The comment says less than length, but actual condition permits equality. Backward traversal may scan the long suffix; the 64-byte comparison limit does not make truncation constant-time in input length. Caller invokes it only for strings longer than64, where at least one Unicode scalar fits.

name: lance_file::versions::v2_2::compression::<Strategy as CompressionStrategy>
behavior: Compute effective field params once. Ordered first-match miniblock choice is explicit uncompressed fixed width, byte-stream split, RLE candidate, bitpacking, raw fixed width, variable width (fallible), fixed packed struct (fallible), raw fixed-size-list. Every None falls through; a helper Err stops selection. If no candidate returns a compressor, NotSupported names data.name(). Successful choice always passes finalize_miniblock_compressor(data, compressor, params), which may itself fail; this is selection, not execution of compression. RLE slot is try_fixed_u8_rle_miniblock. Contextual finalizer only wraps FixedWidth data with requested general compression, returning other compressors unchanged (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:587-598).

name: lance_file::versions::v2_3::writer::Writer::finish
behavior: finish for V2_3 awaits pipeline flush then finish_encoders, constructs descriptor, writes descriptor/global table entries, obtains column-metadata start, writes all column metadata, then column offset table followed by global offset table. num_global_buffers is unchecked len as u32; sink supplies its declared column count. Failures propagate at each step with no local rollback/finished flag. Even a never-initialized lazy writer first flushes the sink before descriptor creation rejects unknown schema. Footer fields in order: u64 LE column_metadata_start, column_metadata_offsets_start, global_buffer_offsets_start; u32 LE global-buffer count and column count; u16 LE major2 and minor3; four-byte MAGIC LANC. Total40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:33-33). Return pipeline rows_written with size from awaited object shutdown. No checksum, terminator retry guard, uniform field-length validation or explicit footer alignment is added. A partial footer or shutdown error does not restore consumed encoders/metadata.

behavior: encode_batch_body reserves batch.data.len+1MiB with unchecked addition, copies full data into BytesMut, optionally clones batch core Schema via TryFrom<&Self>, serializes descriptor and appends it raw, recording one global entry; otherwise globals empty. behavior: finish_encoders returns immediately if no encoders. Otherwise std::mem::take removes all encoders from self, then each writer.finish is awaited with a fresh OutOfLineBuffers planner. Returned external buffers are written raw, unlike batch/flush aligned writes. Planner advances virtual positions including padding but does not insert padding into buffer payloads (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159); correctness of multiple unaligned finish buffers therefore depends on producer invariants. Debug assertion compares emitted count to each encoder num_columns after IO. For each finished column, write final pages then set buffer_position=tell once. Each column buffer is written with trailing padding but recorded position advances only by raw buffer.len; two unaligned buffers can produce recorded offsets different from actual later starts. No seek/check or padding adjustment here. Any-wrap column encoding into Direct, set metadata, increment physical column_index. Final pages carry their own column indices; they are not rewritten to this counter. After all encoders, mismatching physical count panics with expected/actual even in release builds. name: lance_file::writer::structural::EncodingPipeline::verify_field_nullability_where_reachable
behavior: is_initialized tests only schema presence, not encoders or sink state. verify_field_nullability starts recursive validation with every slot reachable. Comments explain null struct parents hide child nulls and dictionary logical nulls may exist without physical key nulls; external Arrow behavior is rationale, while the implementation below explicitly uses logical_nulls. Recursive nullability computes logical_nulls; absent mask means0 offending, top-level uses null_count, otherwise count((NOT validity) AND reachable). A nonnullable field with visible nulls returns InvalidInput naming the field, not the count/path. Empty field.children ends recursion. Counts/masks assume array shape consistent with field. For any non-StructArray with children, zip declared children with ArrayData.child_data, clone/reconstruct each child Array and recurse with reachable=None. Parent reachability is deliberately not propagated across list-like offsets. Zip ignores unmatched tails; this helper does not independently enforce child count/type. It checks all exposed child-data slots, not only referenced list positions. For StructArray, own validity is logical mask or all-set BooleanBuffer of parent length. Child reachability is own AND inherited mask, or own at root. Zip schema children with parent.columns and recurse in order, stopping at first error. Sliced StructArray columns already align to parent window per source comment and local test. Child-count mismatch is not checked here.

name: lance_file::writer::structural::EncodingPipeline::write_batch
behavior: Debug-instrumented write_batch logs dimensions/memory estimate, expects initialized schema, lazily builds ExpectedTypes and checks types, then positional nullability. Zero rows return only after these checks. Each individual batch above u32MAX rows is rejected, despite diagnostic phrasing about whole files; cumulative count uses u64 later. An empty batch can return before missing-name detection in encode_batch. Start OutOfLineBuffers at sink tell/alignment64, synchronously build encoder tasks, write all reserved buffers with trailing padding, flatten tasks into FuturesOrdered. Only then checked_add aggregate u64 rows; overflow returns InvalidInput after encoder mutation and possible buffer IO. On success increment every field counter and aggregate before awaiting page writes. Page/flush failure leaves those counters advanced; no transactional retry guarantee. Per-field increments are unchecked arithmetic.

name: lance_file::writer::structural::EncodingPipeline::write_column
behavior: write_column requires schema presence or InvalidInput mentioning explicit schema (a previously initialized lazy writer also satisfies actual check). Get top-level field by index with contextual bounds error; reject this array length above u32MAX before type/nullability validation. No inference from a bare array. Lazily build ExpectedTypes, check selected column type, then logical nullability; empty arrays return afterward. Encode singleton field with out-of-line planner, write reserved buffers, order tasks, then unchecked-add selected field count and set aggregate rows=max(old aggregate,new field total) before awaiting pages. Other fields unchanged and differing lengths permitted; no cumulative overflow check here. External-metadata initialization alone may leave encoder/count vectors empty and make a later nonempty column write panic on indexing.

name: lance_file::writer::structural::StructuralFileSink::write_column_metadatas
behavior: write_column_metadatas takes all column metadata and spill state out of self before awaits. Active spill flushes/shuts down its writer, opens sidecar for reading, and takes chunk vectors; Pending/None produce no reader. Failure loses these taken in-memory states from the sink and can leave a sidecar object. No retry/rollback guard or explicit sidecar deletion is implemented. For each column in order, Active spill reads every recorded chunk sequentially via unchecked usize range arithmetic, decodes all pages and accumulates one complete column Vec. Replace metadata.pages with that Vec, discarding any pages retained before spill activation/external initialization. Serialize/write whole column, push position. Peak memory still includes full-column pages and serialized bytes plus chunk descriptors; spill does not stream one page into final metadata. No sidecar cleanup after success.

name: lance_file::writer::structural::StructuralFileSink::write_page
behavior: write_page consumes EncodedPage data, records tell before each payload, stores unpadded length and writes with trailing alignment. After all payload bytes, prost Any-wrap Legacy or Structural description without restricting version/grammar. Construct Direct encoding Page with num_rows as length and row_number as priority, then unchecked-cast physical column index to usize. Serialization failure can follow already-written data. On the first page after configuring Pending, take the pending state, asynchronously create a sidecar sized to current num_columns and install Active. Failure/cancellation during creation leaves page_spill None after data was written. Active appends page; None pushes into column_metadata[column_index]; unreachable branches enforce immediately checked private states. Bounds are trusted. Pages retained before spill activation are not copied into sidecar.

For V1 encoding, remove every TOMBSTONE_FIELD_ID then require strictly increasing live IDs (no duplicates); failure is CorruptFile at base_path.join(path) with unsorted/duplicate message. For other encodings require columns.len>=fields.len; extra columns accepted, failure contextual CorruptFile. It does not verify exact file version, nonnegative values, file existence, row count, base IDs or column uniqueness/range. V1 branch allocates a live-ID Vec.

name: lance_table::format::fragment::InternCache<T>::<implementation>
behavior: InternCache starts Small(empty). Small scans for content equality and returns a cloned existing Arc; on miss converts Vec to Arc, inserts a clone, and promotes only when unique entries exceed16 (the17th miss). Promotion drains all stored Arcs into a HashMap. Large performs borrowed slice lookup, returning stored Arc or inserting new Arc. Caches grow without eviction; no interning across the two separate i32 caches. Lookup complexity is linear in unique entries and comparison length before promotion; map hashing/equality still depends on payload contents after it.

behavior: resolve_version_location first asks the external index. On core NotFound it calls default_resolve_version and maps any failure of that resolver to a core NotFound for base@version. It then HEADs the fallback path. Success attempts an onboarding put_if_not_exists using actual size and ETag None; reservation failure merely warns. This is best-effort backfill, not a second arbitration step before serving existing object bytes. The onboarding success returns the requested version, fallback path, actual size/ETag, staging naming heuristic and identity None, even if the store minted an identity during insertion. Raw HEAD NotFound becomes a contextual core NotFound; other errors propagate. Other initial external errors propagate directly. The heuristic unwraps filename, relying on the fallback path constructor to provide one. For an indexed exact-version location, identity Some uses recorded_as_final; a manifest extension uses generic finalized verification. Otherwise it recomputes the staging naming heuristic (unlike latest lookup, which uses the recorded scheme), obtains size by HEAD only if absent, and finalizes using the requested version. This unknown-size staging HEAD has no latest-lookup refetch branch on NotFound. The location identity is assigned after finalization.

name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::copy_via_read_rewrite
behavior: Private copy_via_read_rewrite opens the source GET stream before starting destination multipart upload, allocates a 100 MiB buffer and consumes stream chunks. A stream error attempts upload.abort, ignores abort failure and returns the original stream error. The function returns the object-store result type. Cancellation has no local Drop abort guard, so the explicit error branches do not cover all interrupted uploads. Each input chunk is sliced into the remaining part capacity and copied into the Vec. A full buffer is replaced with a fresh 100 MiB allocation, converted into Bytes and uploaded with a sequential awaited put_part; failure attempts abort and returns the original error. This bounds part buffers, not total memory: the current upstream chunk, in-flight payload and replacement allocation may coexist. Parts are not uploaded in parallel. A remaining nonempty buffer is uploaded as the short final part, with abort-on-error. Empty input proceeds to complete without a part. complete failure also attempts abort and preserves its original error; success returns Ok. No explicit total-byte comparison, checksum, part-count ceiling, abort-error reporting or cancellation cleanup is present; the caller's final HEAD checks only expected size.

name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::finalize_staged
behavior: Public async finalize_staged<S: ExternalManifestStore + ?Sized> accepts an already selected staging path, version, expected size, raw object store and naming scheme. It computes the canonical manifest path, calls copy_or_verify_final_manifest, then constructs a canonical ManifestLocation with Some(size), the observed ETag and identity None. It does not itself acquire or validate the external reservation. Correct use requires the caller to have selected these immutable staging bytes. After the canonical copy succeeds, finalize_staged updates the existing external record to the canonical path/size with ETag None. Any index-update error is warned and swallowed: return the committed canonical location and retain staging for a later helper. Thus external index compaction is subsequent repair work, not rollback authority over the durable canonical object. A failed earlier copy/HEAD still propagates before this branch. Once index publication succeeds, finalize_staged deletes staging. name: lance_table::rowids::index::RowIdIndex::probe
behavior: Private probe returns None for zero fragments or no start <= row ID. partition_point finds the candidate upper bound. An iterative stackless left-to-right DFS uses max-end tree values to prune subtrees, tests FragmentEntry::resolve at leaves, and continues after the first live hit to detect a second. name: lance_table::rowids::RowIdSequenceCursor::extend_range

name: lance_table::transaction::Operation::upsert_key_conflict
behavior: Public upsert_key_conflict allocates four cloned-key Vecs from both operations, then checks left upserts intersect right upserts/deletes OR right upserts intersect left upserts/deletes. Shared delete-only keys are allowed; equal values still conflict; any syntactic upsert followed by deletion is still represented in both lists. replace flags/implicitly deleted keys are not considered. Vec::contains gives quadratic worst-case comparisons plus string costs; short-circuit occurs after all four lists have been built. Predicate is symmetric for ordinary strings. It returns bool with no error, IO, locks or mutation; consumer classifies the conflict.
callers: Contextual lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs1546/1559/2032/2043.
callees: Both key extractors; four Vecs; symmetric upsert-involving overlap via contains.

name: lance_table::utils::stream::<MergeStream as Stream>

Otherwise it rotates past filled slots and polls the next empty slot; a ready task becomes PendingReadBatch, any exhausted input ends output immediately, and Pending returns without polling subsequent missing streams that time. Construction guarantees nonempty streams before indexing/modulo.
